evidence.text: The file page identifies 打-seal.svg as a modern vector drawing of 打 in Shuowen seal-script style and points to the S09107 entry at Chinese Etymology (hanziyuan) as the picture source. It says the SVG representation is public domain and attribution is appreciated. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese characters project
evidence.text: The project says its graphics are freely usable and public domain, with source and author attribution requested as a moral condition. Its categories distinguish transcribed script styles, such as Shuowen seal, from ancient artifact-script traditions such as oracle and bronze. This project-level statement does not substitute for the individual file page's provenance or rights details.
evidence.title: Commons:Ancient Chinese characters project - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The 打-seal.svg page lists related styles including Shang oracle, Shang bronze, Western Zhou bronze, Spring and Autumn bronze, Warring States bronze, Chu slip and silk, Qin slip, Shuowen seal and Shuowen ancient. These are links to project categories, not evidence that each style has an authenticated 打 glyph; the inspected Shang oracle category's displayed files did not include 打.

search_audit.query: Inspect related historical-style links listed on 打-seal.svg for usable 打 candidates
search_audit.outcome: Opened the links exposed by the file page. No separate verified oracle or bronze image of 打 was established; the inspected Shang oracle category's listed media did not include 打. One related category page request returned an internal error.

search_audit.query: Open direct image URL exposed by the Commons file page
search_audit.outcome: The page-linked original URL failed in the web tool with a cache miss; the earlier candidate URL using /0/0d/ was inaccessible via the tool. The Commons HTML page nevertheless exposes the exact direct-link target.

gaps: The linked direct image itself could not be fetched by the web tool (cache miss), so its pixel contents and successful delivery were not verified in this invocation. Its identity and reuse provenance are supported by the inspected Commons file description page.

No additional direct-image candidates for 打 were established from the historical-style links; categories alone do not prove character identity. The file page itself lists styles without proving every linked style contains a glyph of 打. The Commons page also links a hanziyuan S09107 image, but its direct URL and reuse terms were not established here.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; normalized seal-script form associated with the Shuowen entry (received compilation, Eastern Han; specific exemplar date not established)
items.tradition: Shuowen seal script, modern digital redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of 打 in Shuowen seal-script style. The Commons file credits image source S09107 at Chinese Etymology; no specific ancient artifact or manuscript exemplar is identified on the file page.
items.alt: Black seal-style strokes representing 打 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The file page directly identifies the character and script style, names its source entry, and provides a reusable public-domain representation. This is the only candidate supported by an inspected individual file description; it can illustrate the documented seal-script form but should not be presented as an artifact image or proof of a graphic sequence.

limitations.text: The direct file URL exposed by the source page was not fetched successfully by the web tool (cache miss); image contents were not visually inspected during research. Separate oracle or bronze candidates were not established from the inspected linked categories.
